---
title: "Performance"
---

Local measurements of the Python API using the scripts in `benchmarks/`.

## Results

| Measurement | Coverage |
|---|---|
| [1-D arrays](performance/array-1d-benchmarks.qmd) | 11 reducers and their NaN-aware forms, lengths 30–10 million, float32/float64. |
| [Axis reductions](performance/axis-benchmarks.qmd) | Five layouts, including shallow stacks and contiguous last-axis reductions. |
| [Sigma clipping](performance/sigma-clipping.qmd) | Mask, diagnostic, and fused outputs for vectors and axis-0 stacks. |

Performance depends on operation, dtype, layout, and thread settings. NumPy
and Bottleneck can win individual cases; the tables retain those results.
Implementation details are in [How It Gets Fast](performance/max-performance.qmd).

## How To Read The Numbers

Benchmark ratios are reported as `np/rd` and `bn/rd`; values above `1` mean
`reducers` is faster.

The 1-D and axis scripts check reducers against NumPy before timing
(`rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-10` for float64; `rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-5` for float32;
matching NaNs accepted). A reducers mismatch stops the run. Bottleneck is
optional: results that fail the same check are excluded and labelled `n/a`.
Missing implementations use `-`. Sigma-clipping checks are described on its
own page.

These are local timings, not a guarantee across machines or a controlled
comparison against an earlier release. Rerun on the target machine when a
small difference matters.

## Recorded Environment

Recorded **2026-09-08** from **`eb27fc0`**: v0.4.0 plus the subsequent overflow
fix, built with `maturin develop --release --locked --offline`. The package
version still reports `0.4.0`; these are current-checkout results, not
measurements of the published v0.4.0 wheel.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Machine | Apple M4 Pro, macOS 26.6, arm64 |
| Python / NumPy / Bottleneck | 3.13.11 / 2.4.6 / 1.6.0 |
| Rayon / other thread pools | 14 / 1 |
| Grain settings | Built-in defaults; saved tuning disabled |
| Scan / weighted grains | 262144 |
| Median / percentile grains | 1024 |
| 1-D min/max grain | 65536 |

The previous tables used v0.3.2 and tuned variance/minmax grains. Differences
between those tables and these runs cannot be attributed solely to the code.
Full output linked from each benchmark page records the commit, extension
SHA-256, command, resolved grains, and dependency versions.

Set up a project `.venv` with the benchmark dependencies and a release build:

```bash
uv sync --extra dev --extra bench
uv run --no-sync maturin develop --release --locked
```

Use these settings for the commands on each benchmark page:

```bash
export REDUCERS_IGNORE_TUNED_GRAINS=1 RAYON_NUM_THREADS=14
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1
export REDUCERS_BENCH_BUILD_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```

Run benchmarks sequentially on an otherwise idle machine. Clear any
`REDUCERS_*_GRAIN` overrides to reproduce built-in defaults. Set the commit
label only after building that checkout; it is caller-supplied metadata.
